source.title: Towards Predictive, Aligned, and Scalable Robot Learning
source.authors: Peijun Tang; Shangjin Xie; Baifu Huang; Binyan Sun; Haotian Yang; Kuncheng Luo; Weiqi Jin; Shilin Fang; Jianan Wang

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports scaling-related results for robotic action prediction, but does not test the language-model power laws, their extrapolation, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation in the claim.
record.gate_note: Section 4.5 reports training-loss and action-reconstruction trends for two action tokenizers. These are related scaling results, not held-out language-model cross-entropy or a fitted power law. Other tokenizer reconstruction comparisons and semantic-prediction results do not test a claim version and are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Section 4.5, titled 'Alignment and Scaling Laws', compares two action tokenizers over 100k training steps of one fixed-size model on one dataset. It varies neither parameters, data nor compute across scales and fits no power law. It therefore does not test any version, including V5 (other regimes). The word 'scaling' refers to training-loss curves over steps, not to scaling laws.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that progressive pre-alignment of actions with world dynamics, vision and language yields 'improved scaling behavior' for action prediction. Their evidence is a single fixed-scale tokenizer comparison: lower early but higher final BAR loss for Stage 2, with lower decoded errors except gripper. They do not fit or report any power law.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares action tokenizers in robotic action-generation training, rather than testing the original language-model scaling-law recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The BAR-loss comparison changes direction between early training and convergence; decoded reconstruction-error comparisons vary by action dimension, with gripper as the stated exception.

fits_no_version.finding: In robot action-model training at fixed size, the Stage 2 (semantically pre-aligned) tokenizer gives lower early BAR loss but higher final BAR loss than the Stage 1 tokenizer. Its decoded reconstruction errors are lower on all metrics except gripper.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Action-tokenizer pre-alignment changes training-loss trajectories and decoded action error in VLA training.

record.problems: The relevant scaling curves are presented without numerical values in the text, and the study does not fit or report power-law exponents. Its measurements concern robotic action loss and reconstruction, not held-out language-model cross-entropy.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant findings left out. Section 4.5's action-reconstruction baseline comparison and semantic action classification are not scaling-law tests.

untested.parts: Loss versus parameters, tokens or compute over orders of magnitude; no model sizes or data scales are varied.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No architecture-shape sweep at fixed parameters.
No power-law fit in the robotics/action setting.
Downstream task success is not related to scale or loss.
No exponents are fitted, so their dependence on setup or fitting choices is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: The study uses the term 'scaling laws' in its title and section heading without any scale sweep or power-law fit. T6/discusses is appropriate. The paper's other results (VLM benchmarks, real-robot success rates, Table 6 reconstruction, Table 7 probing) do not bear on any version.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; power-law behavior over several orders of magnitude.
Extrapolation from small language-model runs to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation and its trend with compute.
Architecture effects at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds for other modalities or training regimes.
Predictability of downstream task performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted language-model exponents or compute-optimal allocations on setup and fitting choices.
